key_insight: SPHERE learns and reuses a user’s spatial preferences in VR indoor scene generation, turning one-off synthesis into continuous human-AI co-creation.
engineering_relevance: This framework can reduce repetitive manual edits and physical strain in immersive authoring by adapting scene retrieval and layout generation to individual users over time.
method: Extracts persistent preferences from speech and controller-based edits during VR interaction.
Converts raw edits into hierarchical spatial constraints capturing local function and global topology.
Uses human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning to update retrieval policies from final edited scenes.
evidence_signal: A mixed-design user study with 42 participants and an offline ablation showed fewer corrective edits and lower physical demand, with better preference-aligned and geometrically resilient layouts.
watch_item: The approach may depend on high-quality interaction logs and careful constraint design, which could make deployment sensitive to noisy user behavior or overfitting to shallow preferences.
paper_title: SPHERE: Adaptive VR Indoor Scene Generation via LLM-Enhanced Spatial Preference Learning and Human-in-the-Loop RL
